findings.issue_text: [High/security] ClientPermissionsV2.java:79 — canView(client) immediately accepts an all-clients VIEW grant before evaluating the target client’s permissions, bypassing client-specific denials.

[Medium/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.java:88 — canView() excludes the all-clients MANAGE permission, causing administrators with only that permission to fail the inherited client listing check despite being allowed to create clients.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/security] ClientPermissionsV2.java:79 — canView(client) immediately accepts an all-clients VIEW grant before evaluating the target client’s permissions, bypassing client-specific denials.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.java:79, the canView(ClientModel client) method first checks canView() (which includes all-clients VIEW permission) OR canConfigure(client). If either returns true, it returns true. Then it checks hasPermission(client, VIEW) for client-specific permission. This is standard permission logic - having a broader permission (all-clients VIEW) should grant access. The finding claims this 'bypasses client-specific denials', but looking at the hasPermission method and the test cases (testViewUserPermissionDenyByDefault), the system uses Logic.NEGATIVE policies for denials, not separate deny permissions on specific resources. The all-clients permission check is intentional design - if you have permission to view all clients, you can view any client. This is consistent with the V1 implementation pattern and the test cases shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] ClientPermissionsV2.java:88 — canView() excludes the all-clients MANAGE permission, causing administrators with only that permission to fail the inherited client listing check despite being allowed to create clients.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.java, canView() at line 88 returns `canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`. It only checks for VIEW permission on all-clients, not MANAGE. However, canManage() at line 73 checks for MANAGE permission. The issue is that canList() (inherited from parent) calls canView(), and someone with only MANAGE permission on all-clients would pass canManage() but fail canView(). This is inconsistent - if you can manage all clients, you should be able to view/list them. Looking at the parent class pattern and canView(ClientModel client) at line 80 which includes canConfigure(client) check, the all-clients canView() should likely also include hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) for consistency.
